Check out this heated exchange at the NDIS Bill hearing.

The government says employment supports will not be affected.

But when pressed, officials confirmed the reality that many disabled people already know: people use their plans flexibly because life does not fit neatly into funding categories.

A person might need support to do all the things you need to do to get a job.

That support may sit under social and community participation but not be labelled as such because we use our NDIS funding flexibly.

If that funding is cut, which because of this Bill, it will be by 50%, it can affect employment. It will affect whether someone can take up an opportunity at all.

If the government is serious about increasing disability employment, it cannot pass legislation that makes it harder for people to get to the interview, take the job, or keep the supports that make work possible.

The Senate must stop this Bill. It will cause harm.

Thank you Jordon Steele-John for interrogating this dangerous Bill.

It’s their favourite line… ‘we aren’t funding anything in category X because you can use funding flexibly from category Y. 

And then if you get a new job you need to tell your employer ‘will you hold the position for me for 3.5 months while the NDIS processes my change of circumstances reassessment and (hopefully) funds the employment supports.’ 🫠🫠🫠🫠

..and if they get the job, how long will it take to go through the change in situation? The time taken could very much lose the job while waiting....and even if it's reviewed, there's no guarantee that you'll get it. 
So much dignity in begging for necessary supports to earn a living.....

Just dropping this here so you can see the dastardly business these great minds have been working on.

https://cdn.fbsbx.com/v/t59.2708-21/721247374_2170643113735962_6184798261608975825_n.pdf/foi-26-2898-ndis-sustainability-taskforce-establishment.pdf?_nc_cat=110&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=2b0e22&_nc_ohc=PTinY6MsGVIQ7kNvwH7c4E7&_nc_oc=Adqftb4hv_T_mwchDCy4zO6-zh0QLyxzc-_OzssGayDZ6TeHZb12QJdvT0Lj5jwnYTY&_nc_ad=z-m&_nc_cid=0&_nc_zt=7&_nc_ht=cdn.fbsbx.com&_nc_gid=Kdy0-H1sc5pvgrmy6gOaug&_nc_ss=7a338&oh=03_Q7cD5gEFXG-yS1fPWepurbC3WVrNBO4w9zNYSHyXUHC5QpvqGQ&oe=6A2C986B&dl=1

If I am working in a minimum wage job e.g. $25/hr what right do I have to expect that the tax payer subsidize me at the rate of $70/hr?

If the agency cannot see the issues here, it is absolutely mind-boggling to me. I cannot believe the explanations, or lack there of that have been provided.

I would be keen to understand how this aligns with employers’ obligations under the Fair Work Act?. If support is reduced and employers subsequently seek to reduce employees’ working hours as a result of these decisions, is that not fundamentally an employment contract issue? I would certainly think so.

This is what happens when people that have no idea about the disability experience make decisions that impact it. Thank goodness for Jordan John Steele. And others (including yourself Dr George Taleporos (GAICD, PhD) ). 

The problem is the ableism is so deeply entrenched, they don't even realise how contradictory the statements are.

Thank you Jordon Steele-John for your relentless determination to make clear the actual impact these cuts can have not only on individuals participating in community life, but also, on their employment (and in turn, their financial wellbeing).

While like others, I found it hard to believe you had to reiterate the case so many times over, it was a powerful example of just how devastating these indiscriminate cuts could be if implemented in the manner proposed.

Well done on the degree of patience and also pointing out the 'simple' lifestyle needs of all of us when we attend interviews etc. The ndis, is as complex as life itself. It is a highly important scheme in many ways. One of the difficulties the scheme has a deep need for is the clear alignment of living with a disability and having a world that isnt designed for people with disability. When we explore employment of pwd, we very rarely think through the complexities of life and how they impact pwd. I once had a supervisor reprimand me for emailing them to say i would be off work that day due to sickness. I have a stutter which gets worse when stressed, consequently using the phone isnt an option. However the commonwealth agency i was employed at was determined to punish me because i didnt follow the hr policy of needing to phone in non attendance. Its crazy how we develop policy/legislation/ systems and then expect life to fit. Lets change that, people design for people not for boxes.

My social and community support enables me to study my PhD, which I’m hoping will enable me to work again one day. My support workers do not support me to complete my PhD directly. Many of them haven’t studied beyond high school, even at tafe, and I’m not saying that in a derogatory way. I’m saying it because the activities and work that I do for my PhD are far outside the scope of what the average support worker can understand or relate to. They cannot support me directly in this way. 

The REASON my social and community participation funding enables me to complete my PhD is because my supports break the cycle of hyperfixation and overwhelm. They enable me to step away from my intense, cognitive work and complete the basic everyday tasks that MUST be attended to stay alive and healthy. 

My supports ensure I have groceries and medication, they ensure I am moving and active throughout the week, they give me space to express myself and make connections. If not for my social and community supports, I would live my entire life through a computer screen.

If they’re taken away, I would have to drop out of my PhD. These are the consequences the government seem to have no understanding of, because this isn’t their life.
